title: Settings
personalNote: Your personal settings. The owner and PM manage the rest of the project.

general.numberInvalid: Write a whole number above zero.
general.offsetsInvalid: Write hours separated by commas, like 24, 2.
general.timeInvalid: Write the time in 24-hour format, like 07:30.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.body: When the decider gets a reminder, and when a decision escalates to the PM.

staleness.title: Staleness
staleness.body: After this long the item shows as stale and the responsible role gets a reminder.

digests.title: Digests and quiet hours
digests.body: Saving reschedules the digest right away. During quiet hours, push and Telegram wait and arrive together afterwards.

onboarding.title: Reading paths
onboarding.body: What a new member reads on the Onboarding page, per role, in this order.
onboarding.refHint: A doc path, a card key or a link.

project.title: Project
project.body: Every date in Hub is shown in this project’s timezone.
project.name: Name
project.statusHint: Paused is a label for people. Closing, below, stops writes.
project.closedBanner: This project is closed. It stays readable, and nothing can change until it is reopened.
project.detailsBody: What Claude reads in the project brief, and what a new member reads first.
project.repoPathsHint: One absolute path per line. A session in one of them lands on this project.

general.urlInvalid: Each link needs a label and a full URL.
general.pathInvalid: Each folder must be an absolute path, like F:/Goteav/backend.

security.title: Security
security.body: Two-step sign-in is optional unless a role is chosen here. A member holding a chosen role enrols before any page of this project opens.
security.roles: Roles that must use two-step sign-in
security.hint: With none chosen, each member decides for themselves in their profile.

close.sectionBody: Stops writes and keeps everything readable. It can be reopened. Projects are never deleted. Owner only.
close.title: Close this project?
close.body: No card, setting or source can change until an owner reopens it. All of it stays readable.
close.ownerOnly: Only the owner can close the project

link.title: Link a folder
link.body: Registers this folder on the project. On the device that holds it, Hub also accepts the folder’s trust in Claude Code, so a chat there lands on this project with no dialog. It writes that one entry to ~/.claude.json, keeps every other key, and keeps a backup. It happens only when you press the button.
link.folderHint: The full path on that device.
link.noDevice: No device is online. Connect one in {link}.
link.linked: {folder} is now on {project}. A chat there needs no dialog.
link.shapeUnexpected: Hub registered the folder, but changed nothing in Claude Code, because its config file was not in the shape expected. Open Claude Code in this folder and accept the trust dialog once.
link.mcpFailed: Hub registered the folder, but Claude Code refused the setting, so trust was not written. See Settings › Devices.

sources.disableBody: Its repeating job stops and no new cards arrive from it. Its existing cards stay as they are, and you can enable it at any time.

form.name: Source name
form.nameInvalid: Use 2 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
form.nameTaken: A source with this name already exists.
form.nameLocked: A source’s name stays fixed, because its cards keep it.
form.tokenHint: Optional for now. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
form.tokenStored: The token is stored encrypted and cannot be shown.
form.rootHint: Absolute, on the machine running Hub.
form.added: Added {name}. Its first run starts within minutes.
form.localPathHint: Absolute, on the machine running Hub, like F:/Goteav/backend/docs.
form.pathInvalid: Write an absolute path with no “..”.
form.needsRepo: Add a GitHub repo source first: this kind reads through one.

sources.notConnectedBody: Reading GitHub is not on in this release. It needs a GitHub token and the capture worker. Settings stay here until then.
sources.notConnectedDeps: Reads through a GitHub repo source, so it waits for GitHub too.
sources.laggingWhy: The last successful run was {d} ago, over three times its period of {period}.
sources.toDoFailing: Read the error, then fix the source’s settings. It runs again on its next period.
sources.toDoLagging: Check that the worker is running and the source can be reached.
sources.testOk: The folder can be read: {n} files.
sources.testUnavailable: This kind cannot be tested in this release, because reading GitHub is not on yet.
sources.testUnreadable: Hub cannot read this folder. Check the path.
sources.emptyBody: Add a local folder so Hub can index its docs or scan the lab.

roles.title: The seven roles
roles.matrixBody: What each role may do. A member’s Claude Code may do the same, through their token.

cells.V: Routed role, requester or who delivered

roles.specialtyBody: Which roles may take a task of each specialty. This is the release’s fixed rule, not a setting.

rows.card_edit_routing: Edit priority, due date, role, assignee
rows.task_start: Start, submit and finish a task
rows.need_verify: Verify; whoever delivered may, with a note
rows.release_release: Edit and mark a release released
rows.token_manage: Own API tokens: create and revoke

notes.owner: Can do everything, and is the only role that approves redesigns. At least one must stay active.
notes.pm: Receives escalations, and manages members, sources, settings and priorities.
notes.frontend: Frontend work, shared components and ported redesigns.
notes.qa: Tests, and requests changes on redesigns.

tokens.title: My tokens
tokens.intro: These connect your own Claude Code to Hub. A token shows in full once, when you create it, and only its prefix after that.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: The device and the tool, like Claude Code on my laptop.
tokens.nameRequired: Write a name you will recognise later.

canList.mcp: Whatever you may do on the web, by your roles in each project: read, create, edit, decide, verify, approve and delete. The event records that it came through MCP.
canList.hook: Send session facts to Hub, nothing else.

cannotList.mcp: Create tokens, set a source’s secret, or change your profile: those stay on the web.

tokens.onceWarning: You won’t see this token again. Copy it now.
tokens.mcpCommand: Set it up in Claude Code with one command
tokens.packCommand: Or install the team pack, which also adds the skills and hooks
tokens.revokeBody: Anything using it gets a 401 from its next request. This cannot be undone: you would create a new token.
tokens.emptyBody: Create one to connect your own Claude Code to Hub.
tokens.linkCommand: Then in each project’s folder, so a chat there is on this project
tokens.linkHint: hub is packages/team-pack/bin/hub.mjs in the Hub repository until the pack is published.

system.lagBody: Time since the last successful run. It counts as late past three times the run period.
system.failedLoad: The API did not answer the health check.
system.staleWorker: Worker heartbeat stale: the last beat was {rel}. Sources and notifications stop until it returns. Restart the worker service on the host.
system.backupNoneNote: No backup yet. Settings › Backups makes one.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.appendOnly: Append-only: rows are added, never edited or deleted, and they hold no secrets.
audit.rangeInvalid: The start date is after the end date.
audit.noMatchBody: Widen the dates or clear the filters.
audit.emptyBody: Every admin action, decision and delivery shows up here as it happens.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: In this release Hub notifies inside Hub only: the Inbox and the sidebar’s count.
notifications.inAppStatus: Every notification reaches your Inbox, live.

needs.push: Needs HTTPS through Caddy and VAPID keys on the server.
needs.telegram: Needs a Telegram bot and its token on the server.
needs.email: Needs a mail server for notifications. In development, mail is used for invites only.

devices.title: My devices
devices.intro: Each device runs a small bridge that connects out to Hub. It can only work in folders you registered on a project, and you can cut it off here at any time.
devices.emptyBody: Run the command below on a device. On the main machine, pnpm start:local does this for you.
devices.noReport: No report yet. It will check once it is online.

claude_version.bad: Claude Code is too old for Hub

claude_path_version.ok: Claude Code in your terminal is recent enough
claude_path_version.bad: Claude Code in your terminal is older. Hub uses the newest copy, so nothing is stopped

claude_signed_in.bad: Claude Code is not signed in

mcp_server.ok: Hub is set up in Claude Code
mcp_server.bad: Hub is not set up in Claude Code

plugin.bad: The hub plugin is not installed

login_start.ok: The bridge starts when you log in
login_start.bad: The bridge does not start when you log in

vscode.bad: VS Code was not found. Only Open in VS Code needs it

devices.revokeBody: Its bridge is cut off at once, and its Claude Code loses Hub. Connecting it again needs the command and your approval.
devices.connectBody: One command in any terminal. It opens your browser for you to approve, then sets up the bridge, Hub in Claude Code, and the plugin. It is safe to run again. It needs Node 22 or newer.
devices.connectNote: No token to copy and no new terminal. Run the second command on a device to remove all of it.

publishing.title: Reaching Hub from other devices
publishing.intro: Your other devices reach Hub through Tailscale, inside your own private network, and never from the open internet.
publishing.secureOff: Cookies are not Secure yet: they turn on with an https address
publishing.listenAll: Hub listens on every network interface of this machine
publishing.notInstalled: Tailscale is not installed on this machine
publishing.notRunning: Tailscale is installed but not connected
publishing.notServesWeb: Tailscale does not serve Hub's pages yet
publishing.servesApi: Tailscale serves /mcp and /bridge for Claude Code and the bridge
publishing.notServesApi: Tailscale does not serve /mcp and /bridge yet
publishing.notMatches: HUB_PUBLIC_URL is not the tailnet address yet
steps: Install Tailscale on this machine and sign in.
Run this here, then put the two lines it prints in .env and restart Hub:
Turn on two-step sign-in (TOTP) in your profile.
On the other device: install Tailscale, sign in to the same account, and open Hub's address.
Pair its bridge with the command under Connect a new device.
publishing.guide: The full steps are in docs/13-operations.md, "Other devices over Tailscale".

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Hub on this machine is the only copy of its knowledge, so it backs itself up every night: the database, with every document revision, and the current text of each document Hub wrote. Never the .env file or any secret.
backups.emptyBody: The first one runs tonight, or now with Back up now.
backups.missingNote: Its folder is no longer on the disk.
backups.keepHint: A kept backup is never removed by the keep rule.
backups.deleteBody: Its folder is removed from the disk, and this cannot be undone. The line stays in the history.
backups.deleteKeptBody: This backup is kept. Its folder is removed from the disk, and this cannot be undone. The line stays in the history.
backups.lowDisk: The backup drive is low on space: {free} free of {total}. Free some space or choose another folder.
backups.disk: {free} free of {total} on the backup drive
backups.scheduleHint: At this time on this machine's clock ({zone}). If Hub is off then, it backs up as soon as it is back.
backups.keepHelp: The newest ones stay; older ones are removed. Kept backups don't count and stay forever. Default: 14.
backups.folderHint: Outside every Git repository, so a backup never ends up in a commit.
backups.restoreBody: There is no restore button: stop Hub, then run this with the folder of the backup you want. It asks you to type the database's name first.
